long_biography.plain_text:
Sales shaped Thomas Haffa's professional identity before he became a media proprietor. After selling cars and IBM equipment, he joined Leo Kirch's group, where he built its home-video operation and later managed merchandising and music publishing. Leaving in 1989, he used an Alfred J. Kwak animation licence to establish EM.TV and link children's programmes with consumer products.

EM.TV's stock-market flotation turned a specialist rights business into one of Germany's most visible media groups. Haffa expanded through programme libraries and entertainment assets before leaving the chief executive role in 2001. He subsequently moved into business aviation and now serves as president and managing director of Air Independence. The role has kept him in private-company operations outside broadcasting.
